doc.title: Harry Edison — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: Road tales, then Cleveland, St. Louis and Harlem
title: Fitting into the Millinder band; reading skills
summary: He knew Tab Smith and Harold Arnold, found Lucky a great director, and credits Jeter-Pillars for teaching him to read.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: How did you fit in as a youngster, this was your first real name band, how did you fit in with Lucky’s band?
Naturally, they had a boy in there from St. Louis, Tab Smith, I knew him. And I knew Harold Arnold who enticed me to go to New York on this fake ticket under somebody else’s

name. But I was still scared of Lucky, the way he would talk. He didn’t know anything about music, one note from the other, but he was a great director. He would hear something arranged one time, he would know where he wanted the dynamics put. As you followed him, it was a beautiful show.
Did you find that your reading skills were up to the job at that point?

After going with Jeter-Pillars band, they had music. We played in St. Louis at this Plantation Club, they had big shows. They had chorus girls and they would have different acts, coming in, big acts come that, we had music. They used to take a lot of time to show guys, to show me how to read this and read that.
So by the time you got with Millinder, you were pretty knowledgeable…
